correctness.rationale: Reconstruct exact pulse-periodic DFE solution and Fourier first variation q1=-s0/[T(k+i omega)]. Eliminate exposed state to obtain Hill equation, take positive Floquet solution, and apply invertible periodic Riccati operator D+g. First mixed coefficient is -K cos(omega tau+arctan(omega/k)); cross-harmonic damping gives the nontrivial multiplier (1-2B/(g^2+omega^2))>0. Analyticity and independent epsilon=0/eta=0 phase invariances factor out epsilon*eta and give uniform C2 remainder, so a C2 perturbation of cosine has precisely two extrema. Standalone numerical integration directly verifies representative mixed coefficients and phase separation; no infinite proof is inferred from finite checks.

originality.rationale: Scientific claim is the explicit mixed epsilon-eta SEIRS *matrix* Floquet coefficient, strictly positive strength and universal leading unique minimizing phase. Full motivating 2024 article reports numerical favorable phase, not this theorem. Earlier scalar SIR seasonal vaccination optimization is acknowledged; the source's arbitrary-pulse or finite-amplitude observations do not imply the two-compartment Riccati coefficient or exact small-amplitude uniqueness. The 2005 SEIRS and 2014 impulsive SEIR threshold works do not visibly cover it. Two plausible primary full papers remained inaccessible; priority risk remains specifically documented, and absolute literature completeness is not asserted.
residual_risks: The original 2014 Onyango–Müller full text could not be obtained, so a stronger hidden SIR perturbation lemma cannot be categorically excluded, despite no directly known two-stage SEIRS theorem.
The 2019 constrained time-varying SEIR optimal-control full paper was not accessible; its abstract indicates a materially different problem, but full-text overlap remains unverified.
Other exact Floquet perturbation results might contain a mathematically stronger general theorem not indexed by title or abstract.
The finite-amplitude optimal phase may differ substantially; the result does not certify nonlinear case reduction.

value.rationale: The 2024 SEIRS seasonal numerical study reports weakly preferred vaccine timing among four candidate phases but offers no quantitative optimization mechanism. The exact analytic leading phase and existence/uniqueness criterion explain *why* the rising-inflection time is close to optimal, distinguish the fraction of susceptibles vaccinated from numbers of doses, and show a nontrivial universality across arbitrarily different exposed/recovery rates. The result provides interpretable mathematical prediction and falsifiable local linear-invasion optimization, rather than a trivial endpoint or mere numerical check.
